title: Genetic markers to enable selection of cork oak and holm oak trees tolerant to drought and Phytophthora cinnamomi
content:
Abstract
Prolonged drought events and root rot caused by Phytophthora cinnamomi (Pc) are the main factors triggering tree mortality in cork oak (Quercus suber L.) and holm oak (Quercus ilex L.). Identifying trees tolerant to low water availability and invasive pathogens is essential for climate-smart forestry. Molecular breeding approaches using genetic markers to aid selection offer promising alternatives to speed up traditional tree breeding cycles. We phenotyped 12 718 Q. suber and Q. ilex seedlings from 18 Spanish populations and identified those with the most contrasting tolerance to drought and Pc. Nineteen expressed sequence tag-simple sequence repeat markers associated with tolerance to drought stress and Pc infection were selected, and their transferability and polymorphism in 108 Q. suber and 112 Q. ilex trees were assessed. Markers identified as being under positive selection under drought (FIR059 and Qr0044) and Pc pressure (CcPT_0014) may confer a fitness benefit to oak trees in sites experiencing forest decline. Markers FIR059, FIR080, FIR094, GOT045, Qr0044 and PIE102 were significantly involved in discriminating seedlings and adults with different drought tolerances, and CcPT_0004, CcPT_0009, CcPT_0021, CsPT_0005, CsPT_0006 and CsPT_0021 were significantly involved in discriminating seedlings and adults with different Pc tolerance. These markers should be included as candidates for use in marker-assisted selection of Q. suber and Q. ilex individuals tolerant to water stress and Pc.
